# build-roadmap-item

One item, start to finish: **gate, notes, spec, code, docs, checks, report.** Asking for an item authorizes **implementation of that one Ready item** and nothing else. It never authorizes a deploy, a migration on a real database, a merge, or another item.

Notes live in `../../.work/<ID>.md` (outside every git repo, so never committed). The platform docs are at `../../mennara-document/mennara-platform`.

## 1. Resume before reading anything

If `../../.work/<ID>.md` exists, read it first and continue from its **Next step**. Trust what it records; re-check only the lines under "To verify". Do not re-read specs, standards or files the notes already settle.

## 2. Read the item cheaply

Read only the item's row, not the whole roadmap:

```bash
grep -n '| <ID> ' ../../mennara-document/mennara-platform/docs/delivery/roadmap.md
```

Take: item text, **status**, "Needs", repo. Then find its capability row in `../../mennara-document/mennara-platform/docs/catalog/<app>.md` (`grep -n '<ID>' ../../mennara-document/mennara-platform/docs/catalog/*.md`) for the spec link and rule IDs.

## 3. Gate (stop here if it fails)

| Status | Do |
|---|---|
| **Ready** | Continue. The owner's request is the implementation authorization for this item. |
| **Blocked** | Stop. Report the owner question from "Needs". Do not build around it. |
| **Later** | Stop. Name the item it waits on. |
| **Done** | Stop. Link its row in `done.md`. |

Also stop and report (never choose silently) when: the spec conflicts with a newer owner-confirmed requirement; the item belongs to a different repo than the current one (name the repo); the work needs a real-database migration, a deploy, or a secret.

## 4. Spec before code

Read only the rules the catalog row names, plus that spec's Current state. No spec for the behavior? Write the rules first with `change-spec` / `new-feature` (status stays Draft, rules marked proposed), then code. Never invent a requirement.

## 5. Write the notes (then keep them current)

Create `../../.work/<ID>.md` (make the `.work` folder if it is missing) with the template at the end. Overwrite, do not append. Keep it under 40 lines, facts only (paths, SHAs, command results), no secrets. Update it after every milestone and before ending a session.

## 6. Reuse first, then build

Before writing any component, request, text or helper, run the repo's `shared-first` skill if it has one, and search the repo for an existing owner of the concern. Record what you found under "Reuse found". Duplicated logic or UI used by a second place is **not copied**: reuse it, or add it to the shared package with that package's own change.

## 7. Implement with this repo's skills

Apply every skill in this repo's `.claude/skills/` (structure, code quality, UI and tokens, shared packages as they exist). Rules that always apply:
- One logical change. A pure move or rename is a separate commit from a behavior change.
- Remove code that the change made unused, and code in the files you touch that is proven unused (see the code-quality skill). Nothing else.
- Never simplify away a security check (CSRF, session binding, replay protection, permission checks, audit).

## 8. Update the docs as you go

In the platform repo (a separate change from the code repo):
- Behavior rules changed: `change-spec` (rule edit plus a change-log row). No progress notes in a spec.
- Capability row: set **Built** and **Work** with `sync-catalog`.
- Repo layout changed: refresh its page in `docs/overview/current-state/`.
- Roadmap status and `done.md`: **only with evidence, after merge and CI** (`record-done`). Never mark Done before that.

## 9. Check

Run the repo's checks from its `CLAUDE.md`, exactly as CI does. Report failures verbatim. Never weaken or delete a test to pass. In the platform repo also run `check-links.py` and `check-catalog.py`.

## 10. Report and stop

Use: **Result, Changes, Verification, Issues**. List the docs updated and the docs still to update. Set the notes' status to "ready for PR". Do **not** commit, push, merge, deploy or migrate unless the owner asks for that step. After merge: run `record-done`, then delete the notes file.

## Notes template

```
# <ID> - <item text>
Repo: <name>   Branch: <name>   Base SHA: <sha>
Gate: Ready (checked <date>)   Spec: <path> rules <ids>
Decisions: - <one line each>
Reuse found: - <package: component/function>
Files changed: - <path> - <why>
Docs: [ ] spec  [ ] catalog  [ ] current-state  [ ] roadmap/done (after merge)
Checks: <command> -> pass|fail (<date>)
Next step: <one line>
To verify: <anything the next session must re-check>
```
